newsitem.title: USA: Roman Catholic Archbishop of Seattle dies.
newsitem.headline: Roman Catholic Archbishop of Seattle dies.

text.p: The Roman Catholic Archbishop of Seattle, Thomas Murphy, died on Thursday after suffering a brain haemorrhage, the archdiocese said.

Murphy, 64, was diagnosed with leukaemia last December and was admitted to the hospital for 39 days for chemotherapy, Jim Britt, a spokesman for the archdiocese, said. He returned to a full schedule and "had been doing pretty well until last week," Britt said.

Murphy fell ill last week while travelling to a meeting of Catholic bishops in Kansas City. He returned to Seattle and was admitted to the Providence Seattle Medical Centre last Friday night, Britt said.
He began undergoing chemotherapy on Tuesday but suffered a cerebral haemorrhage on Wednesday evening. "He was put on life support and passed away this morning," Britt said.

"Archbishop Murphy died surrounded by members of his staff and some of his close friends. His was a peaceful, prayerful death and the archbishop was sent out of this life surrounded by prayer and song," the archdiocese said in a statement.

Washington state Gov. Gary Locke said he was terribly saddened by Murphy's death. "He was a tremendous person, great leader and a public conscience for all people in our state," he said in a statement.

Murphy, born in Chicago Oct. 3, 1932, was ordained to the priesthood in 1958 and was appointed bishop of the Diocese of Great Falls, Montana in July 1978. He assumed office as Archbishop of Seattle on August 21, 1991.
